title: Role Accelerator Stitch + Async Onboard Checklist
body:
Context:
This is a lightweight playbook for closing the gap between offer-acceptance and week-4 impact for IC and manager hires. The goal: stitch recruiting, hiring manager, recruiting coordinator and a cross-functional buddy into an asynchronous checklist so new hires can move forward even when calendar time is scarce.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Recruiting -> offer handoffs often lose contextual nuance (edge-case tech constraints, short-term deliverables).
- Hiring managers rarely have full calendar availability to orchestrate day-zero details.
- New hires cold-start slower when initial tasks aren’t queued/permissioned ahead of arrival.
- Small teams at Redwood need a predictable 30-day ramp with minimal synchronous meetings.

High-level outcomes (30-day success metrics):
- New hire completes first PR or product spec review within 14 days.
- Buddy verifies 5 onboarding touchpoints done by day 10.
- Hiring manager confirms ramp wishlist and first two deliverables scheduled in sprint backlog.
- No access-related blockers persist past day 3.

Roles & responsibilities (stitch):
- Recruiting coordinator (RC): schedule baseline calendar invites, create account checklist, upload offer packet to candidate record.
- Hiring manager (HM): publish 30-day impact wishlist, 1:1 cadence, assign initial ticket(s).
- Buddy (peer): day-zero triage, workspace walkthrough, 2-week async check-ins.
- People Ops (POps): validate security/KMS access, run payroll/KYC and run the onboarding triage template.
- New hire: complete preboarding micro-tasks in the shared checklist doc.

Pre-Start (offer accepted -> day 0) checklist (RC owner unless noted):
- Send preboarding doc with short tasks (account setup links, org chart snippet, Slack intro template).
- Create accounts (Gmail, Slack, Okta) and add to core channels: #company-all, #eng-general, team channel.
- Request infra access: GitHub teams, cloud-project read-only, model-serving sandbox. (POps verify security scopes)
- Add initial sprint tickets: HM to create 2 bite-sized tickets with acceptance criteria.
- Buddy assigned and briefed: buddy should add a 30–60 minute day-zero async note in the shared doc.
- Equipment order placed and tracked (if physical) with ETA.

Day 0 (owner: Buddy + RC):
- Send a short welcome message in Slack + calendar invite for 30-min async orientation (recording + notes).
- Provide jump-start doc: minimal repo list, runbook for local dev, model weights location, common infra gotchas.
- Verify access: HM/Buddy tick through account access matrix (GitHub, infra, confluence).
- New hire completes short "first-commit checklist" items (repo clone, tests run, linter pass).

First week (day 1–7) async-first items (owner: HM/Buddy):
- HM posts 3 immediate learning priorities and one impact task in the team board.
- Buddy posts two short screencasts: workspace layout + debugging tip for local environment.
- People Ops runs a 10-min asynchronous compliance check-in via form.
- New hire leaves a 1-paragraph learning plan in the shared doc (what they’ll focus on week 1).

Interview rubric to inform hiring signals (used by hiring panels; HM + Recruiting lead to iterate):
Scoring: 1 (no signal) — 5 (clear strength). Panel should capture evidence, timebox 45–60m per loop.
Competency anchors:
- System design / architecture thinking (for infra/serving/runtime roles): explains trade-offs, latency/cost reasoning, fallback strategies.
- Product judgment: identifies user/business impact and can write a short acceptance test.
- Code fluency: writes idiomatic code, picks correct abstractions, explains edge cases.
- Collaboration & async communication: writes clear PR descriptions, documents decisions, shares meeting notes.
- On-call & reliability instincts: triage steps, postmortem framing, SLO/signal awareness.
Rubric template (quick copy):
- 5: provides crisp, documented example; quantifies tradeoffs; suggests practical mitigations; has shipped similar systems.
- 4: strong technical answer, minor gaps in deployment/ops detail.
- 3: acceptable for IC level with training; needs mentorship to reach autonomy.
- 2: partial answer, missed core assumptions.
- 1: unsafe/insufficient.
Panel logistics & tips:
- One interviewer focuses explicitly on async communication: give candidate a short doc exercise (write a 10-line runbook).
- Use a shared rubric sheet during debrief; capture specific evidence snippets (code lines, tradeoff rationale).
- After offer, capture 3 tactical notes for HM in the post-interview handoff section on candidate record.

Hiring plan template (recruiting + HM shared):
- Target timeline: sourcing (2–4 weeks) -> interviews (1–2 weeks) -> decision & offer (3–7 days) -> notice & start (2–6 weeks).
- Panel composition: 2 technical, 1 cross-functional, 1 hiring manager, 1 recruiter coordinator (optional).
- Diversity sourcing channels: list specific target communities and 1 outreach owner.
- On-call readiness expectation: clearly stated in job posting if role requires on-call in first 6 months.

First 30-day ramp (HM + Buddy + POps):
Week 1: unblock infra, complete first-commit checklist, pair on first ticket, write learning plan.
Week 2: own a small bug/feature, present short demo to team (15m), check-in async with manager.
Week 3: broader codebase navigation, pair with cross-team engineer, create first doc PR (runbook or postmortem).
Week 4: deliver first acceptance-criteria-complete ticket, retrospective with HM on ramp blockers.

Async communication patterns (best practices):
- Use the "async status" template in the shared doc: Yesterday / Today / Blockers / Help needed. Keep to 3 bullets each.
- For infra access requests, include the exact resource path + TTL + justification; avoid vague asks.
- Use time-stamped screencasts for environment issues instead of long meetings.

Common blockers & mitigations (notes):
- Blocker: Access denied to model weights or dataset. Mitigation: POps pre-create read-only presigned links and include TTL.
- Blocker: Local dev environment fails on binary dependency. Mitigation: provide a prebuilt container image and a small demo commit that verifies build works.
- Blocker: No initial tickets. Mitigation: HM must create at least two small tickets with clear acceptance criteria before start.

Quick templates to paste in docs / Slack:
- Slack intro (RC): "Hi @team, please welcome NAME, starting DATE, role. Buddy is @buddyname — please add helpful links and a +1 for pairing in week 1."
- Post-interview handoff note (recruiter -> HM): 3 tactical notes: "(1) ramp wishlist, (2) known gaps, (3) suggested first-ticket idea".

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we guarantee hardware sandbox access for private deployments before day 0? (POps owning pull).
- Should we require a recorded 20-min overview from HM for all hires? Pilot with serving-runtime team first.
- Create an automated preboarding checklist that wires into the hiring tracker (JIRA/GSheet) — assign to @Elliot.

Appendix: short checklist (one-line items that can be ticked)
- Offer accepted and signed
- Equipment ordered
- Accounts provisioned (okta/slack/github)
summary: Playbook and practical checklist to accelerate new-hire impact via a stitched, async onboarding flow. Includes an interview rubric, hiring plan template, and a 30-day ramp map.
